speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; can you tell me exactly when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and was it triggered by an injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any immediate deformity or "snap" at the time of the injury, and is the finger currently deviated or difficult to straighten? Can you move the finger up and down, and where exactly is the pain most intense?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the inability to flex the distal joint and the mechanism of injury, do you feel pain or a "pop" specifically at the fingertip when I try to gently bend it down? Also, does the finger appear shorter than usual or have a drooping tip?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your inability to flex the fingertip and the football injury mechanism, this sounds like a mallet finger. I need to confirm the bone involvement, so REQUEST TEST: Right Ring Finger X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray_of_the_Right_Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the X-ray shows no fracture, this confirms a soft tissue injury consistent with an extensor tendon rupture. I will now proceed to provide you with the appropriate splinting instructions for recovery. DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
